extracted.intended_audience: applicants and holders of new drug applications and abbreviated new drug applications; drug manufacturers/distributors; regulatory counsel
extracted.subtask_description: Regulatory standards and procedural requirements governing FDA notices of opportunity for hearing, grounds and procedures for withdrawal or suspension of NDAs and ANDAs, required submissions to support hearing requests, and related determinations (e.g., reasons for voluntary withdrawal, relisting).

rubrics_metrics.name: Failure to maintain required records or reports (§314.150(b)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: The applicant has failed to establish a system for maintaining required records, or has repeatedly or deliberately failed to maintain required records or to make required reports under sections 505(k) or 507(g) and §§314.80, 314.81, or 314.98, or has refused to permit access to, copying or verification of, its records.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FDA may notify the applicant (and others manufacturing/distributing identical/related/similar products) and afford an opportunity for hearing on a proposal to withdraw approval if this ground is found.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inadequate manufacturing methods, facilities, or controls (§314.150(b)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: Based on new information evaluated with evidence available at approval, the methods used in, or facilities and controls used for, manufacture, processing, and packing are inadequate to ensure identity, strength, quality, and purity and were not made adequate within a reasonable time after written notice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ground supports proposal to withdraw approval; FDA evaluates new information together with approval record.

rubrics_metrics.name: False or misleading labeling not corrected (§314.150(b)(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: On the basis of new information evaluated with evidence available at approval, the drug's labeling, based on a fair evaluation of all material facts, is false or misleading in any particular and was not corrected by the applicant within a reasonable time after written notice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Labeling issues revealed by new information can be grounds for withdrawal if not corrected after notice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Failure to comply with section 510(j)(2) notice requirements (§314.150(b)(4))
rubrics_metrics.description: The applicant has failed to comply with the notice requirements of section 510(j)(2) of the act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Noncompliance with statutory notice obligations may justify withdrawal procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Failure to submit required bioavailability/bioequivalence data (§314.150(b)(5))
rubrics_metrics.description: The applicant has failed to submit bioavailability or bioequivalence data required under part 320 of this chapter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Omission of required BA/BE data can be grounds for withdrawing approval.

rubrics_metrics.name: Omission of investigations or other pertinent information (§314.150(b)(6))
rubrics_metrics.description: The application does not contain an explanation of the omission of a report of any investigation sponsored by the applicant, or an explanation of omission of other information pertinent to evaluation that the applicant received or otherwise obtained from any source.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to explain omitted investigations or information material to evaluation may support withdrawal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Noncompliance with Good Laboratory Practice for essential nonclinical studies (§314.150(b)(7))
rubrics_metrics.description: Any nonclinical laboratory study described in the application that is essential to show safety was not conducted in compliance with good laboratory practice regulations in part 58 and no reason for the noncompliance was provided, or differences do not support validity of the study.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: GLP noncompliance for essential studies, without justification, may justify withdrawal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Noncompliance with human subject protections for clinical investigations (§314.150(b)(8))
rubrics_metrics.description: Any clinical investigation involving human subjects described in the application, subject to IRB regulations (part 56) or informed consent regulations (part 50), was not conducted in compliance so that rights or safety of subjects were not adequately protected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Violations of IRB/consent protections that compromise safety/rights are grounds for withdrawal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Refusal to permit inspection or submit reserve samples for BA/BE studies (§314.150(b)(9))
rubrics_metrics.description: The applicant or contractor that conducted a BA/BE study described in §320.38 or §320.63 refuses to permit inspection of facilities or records relevant to the study by authorized HHS officers or refuses to submit reserve samples of drug products used in the study when requested by FDA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refusal to cooperate with inspections or to provide reserve samples for critical studies can lead to withdrawal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inconsistency of ANDA labeling with listed drug (§314.150(b)(10))
rubrics_metrics.description: The labeling for the drug product that is the subject of an abbreviated new drug application is no longer consistent with that for the listed drug referred to in the ANDA, except for differences approved in the ANDA or those resulting from (i) a patent issued after approval of the ANDA, or (ii) exclusivity accorded to the listed drug after ANDA approval that do not render the product less safe or effective for remaining nonprotected uses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Label divergence from the listed drug (outside approved or permitted patent/exclusivity differences) may be a ground for withdrawal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant-requested withdrawal treated as waiver of hearing (§314.150(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: FDA will withdraw approval if the applicant requests withdrawal because the drug is no longer being marketed, provided none of the conditions in paragraphs (a) and (b) apply. FDA considers a written request for withdrawal under this paragraph to be a waiver of an opportunity for hearing. Withdrawal under this paragraph is without prejudice to refiling.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Voluntary requests for withdrawal normally waive hearing rights and do not bar future refiling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Voluntary removal with waiver and publication of summary (§314.150(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: FDA may notify an applicant that a potential problem is sufficiently serious to request waiver of hearing to permit FDA to withdraw approval and remove the product; if applicant agrees, FDA will withdraw approval in a Federal Register notice containing a brief summary of agency's and applicant's views.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Voluntary removal negotiated with FDA results in FR notice summarizing both sides rather than formal finding under paragraph (b).

rubrics_metrics.name: Withdrawal of an ANDA when listed drug approval is withdrawn (§314.151(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: An ANDA approved under §314.105(d) may be withdrawn when FDA withdraws approval of the listed drug referred to in the ANDA under §314.150(a) or §314.151. Holders of ANDAs have a right to notice and opportunity to respond; published notice of opportunity for hearing will identify all ANDAs subject to withdrawal if the listed drug is withdrawn.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ANDA holders are entitled to notice and an opportunity to respond; published notices will identify affected products.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice and participation procedures for ANDA holders (§314.151(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: The published notice of opportunity for hearing on withdrawal of the listed drug will serve as notice to holders of identified ANDAs of the grounds; holders may submit written comments and, if a hearing is granted, may participate as nonparty participants per §12.89.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ANDA holders must use the notice to submit comments and may have limited participation rights at hearing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initial decision, objections, limited oral hearing, and final decision process for ANDAs (§314.151(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: If an ANDA holder timely submits comments but cannot participate in a hearing, FDA will issue an initial decision responding to comments and stating whether there are grounds to withdraw; ANDA holders have 30 days to submit written objections; FDA may hold a limited oral hearing to resolve dispositive factual issues; initial decisions become final after 30 days if no objections; timely objections are reviewed in a final decision which constitutes final agency action and is reviewable judicially.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Process creates an administrative record (comments, initial decision, evidence, objections, hearing transcript) which becomes the basis for final agency action; documents will be publicly available per §10.20(j).

rubrics_metrics.name: Exemption of specific ANDA from withdrawal if grounds not applicable (§314.151(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: If FDA determines, based on information submitted by an ANDA holder, that the grounds for withdrawal of the listed drug are not applicable to a particular ANDA, the final decision will state that approval of that ANDA is not withdrawn.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ANDA holders can present information showing listed-drug grounds don't apply to their product; FDA will explicitly preserve those ANDAs if justified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication of notice of withdrawal (§314.152)
rubrics_metrics.description: If FDA withdraws approval of an application or ANDA, FDA will publish a notice in the Federal Register announcing the withdrawal. If withdrawn under §314.150(a) or §314.151, the notice will announce removal from the list of approved drugs and satisfy §314.162(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Withdrawal is publicly announced in the Federal Register and coordinated with list removal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suspension of ANDA approval (§314.153(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: The approval of an ANDA shall be suspended for the stated period when: (1) the Secretary suspends approval of the listed drug under imminent hazard authority; (2) the agency concludes risk of continued marketing/use is inappropriate pending proceedings to withdraw or suspend; or (3) a final decision states the ANDA is suspended because the listed drug was withdrawn from sale for safety/effectiveness or suspended. Suspension takes effect on the date stated and remains until marketing resumes or withdrawal not for safety/effectiveness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Suspension may follow listed-drug suspension, risk determinations, or final decisions; effect and duration are specified in the decision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedures when listed drug voluntarily withdrawn for safety/effectiveness (§314.153(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: If a listed drug is voluntarily withdrawn and FDA determines withdrawal was for reasons of safety/effectiveness, FDA will send each affected ANDA holder the initial decision setting forth reasons; ANDA holders have 30 days to present comments and information; FDA will consider comments and respond in a final decision; FDA may hold limited oral hearings to resolve dispositive factual issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Final decision ordinarily suspends all affected ANDAs and results in FR publication and filing with Dockets Management Staff; FDA may exempt specific ANDAs if reasons are not relevant to their safety/effectiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approval of previously refused, suspended, or withdrawn application upon new data (§314.160)
rubrics_metrics.description: FDA may, on its own initiative or upon applicant request, approve an application or ANDA previously refused, suspended, or withdrawn on the basis of new data; FDA will publish a notice announcing the approval.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: New data can cure prior deficiencies; approvals and notices are published in the Federal Register.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determination whether voluntary withdrawal was for safety/effectiveness reasons (§314.161(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: A determination whether a listed drug voluntarily withdrawn from sale was withdrawn for safety or effectiveness reasons may be made at any time after withdrawal but must be made: (1) prior to approving an ANDA that refers to the listed drug; (2) whenever a listed drug is voluntarily withdrawn and ANDAs referring to it have been approved; and (3) when a person petitions under §§10.25(a) and 10.30.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timing requirements ensure FDA addresses safety/effectiveness status before approving ANDAs or when prompted by petitions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition process for determination of withdrawal reasons (§314.161(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: Any person may petition under §§10.25(a) and 10.30 for a determination whether a listed drug has been voluntarily withdrawn for safety/effectiveness reasons; petition must contain all evidence available to the petitioner concerning the reason the drug was withdrawn from sale.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petitions must be supported by all available evidence; FDA will act on petitions per administrative rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication and proceedings after determination of withdrawal reasons (§314.161(c)-(e))
rubrics_metrics.description: If FDA determines the listed drug was withdrawn for safety/effectiveness reasons, FDA will publish a notice (except as provided elsewhere); if ANDAs are subject to suspension FDA will initiate proceedings in accordance with §314.153(b); a drug determined withdrawn for safety/effectiveness will be removed from the list but may be relisted if marketing resumes or withdrawal is not for safety/effectiveness; FDA will publish notice of relisting and reinstate suspended ANDAs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determinations drive removal/relisting from the approved drug list and associated proceedings affecting ANDAs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Removal of a drug from the list (§314.162(a)-(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: FDA will remove a previously approved new drug product from the list for the period stated when: (1) FDA withdraws or suspends approval of an NDA or ANDA under §314.150(a) or §314.151 or imminent hazard authority for the same period; or (2) FDA issues a final decision that the listed drug was withdrawn from sale for safety/effectiveness reasons or suspended until FDA determines withdrawal has ceased or is not for safety/effectiveness. FDA will publish FR notices announcing removal and relisting when appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Removal and relisting are coordinated with withdrawal/suspension proceedings and Federal Register notices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adulteration and misbranding provisions apply to approved drugs (§314.170)
rubrics_metrics.description: All drugs, including those FDA approves under section 505 and this part, are subject to adulteration and misbranding provisions in sections 501, 502, and 503 of the act; FDA may regulate approved new drugs by regulations issued under these sections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Approval does not exempt a drug from general adulteration/misbranding law and related regulatory actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of opportunity for hearing must state reasons and proposed grounds (§314.200(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director of CDER will give the applicant and all other persons who manufacture or distribute identical/related/similar products notice and an opportunity for a hearing on proposals to refuse approval or withdraw approval under section 505(e); the notice will state the reasons for the action and the proposed grounds for the order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notice must identify grounds and reasons; it can be general or specific (see (a)(1)).

rubrics_metrics.name: General vs specific notice content (§314.200(a)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: The notice may be general (summarizing in a general way the information resulting in the notice) or specific (referring to specific statutory/regulatory requirements not met or providing detailed description and analysis of specific facts resulting in the notice).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FDA has discretion on level of specificity in notices; specificity affects the nature of responses and submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication and 30-day deadline to request hearing (§314.200(a)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: FDA will publish the notice in the Federal Register and state that the applicant and other persons subject to the notice who wish to participate in a hearing have 30 days after publication to file a written notice of participation and request for hearing. Failure to file within 30 days waives the opportunity for a hearing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strict 30-day filing deadline applies unless notice provides otherwise; waiver is automatic if missed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Responsibility to review Federal Register notices and request for applicability opinion (§314.200(a)(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: Every manufacturer/distributor must review every notice of opportunity for hearing published in the Federal Register to determine applicability to their products. Any person may request an opinion of applicability by writing to the Division of New Drugs and Labeling Compliance within 30 days; eligibility for hearing opportunity depends on timely request for opinion—the time to file an appearance and request begins on receipt of FDA's opinion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entities must monitor FR notices and may seek FDA opinion to clarify applicability; requesting an opinion extends timing for filing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methods of providing notice (§314.200(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: FDA will provide notice to persons who submitted an application or ANDA by delivering in person or sending by registered/certified mail to the last address in the application; persons who did not submit an application/ANDA but are subject to notice under §310.6 will receive notice by publication in the Federal Register.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Direct delivery to applicants/ANDA holders; others are reached via FR publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing requirements for notice of participation and supporting studies/comments (§314.200(c)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: A person wishing to participate must file with Dockets Management Staff: (i) within 30 days after publication (or receipt of FDA opinion) a written notice of participation and request for hearing; and (ii) within 60 days after publication (unless a different period specified), the studies on which the person relies to justify a hearing as specified in paragraph (d). Raw data may be incorporated by reference if previously submitted to FDA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Two-step filing: notice of participation within 30 days and supporting studies within 60 days (unless notice changes timeframe).

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitations on consideration of late-submitted data (§314.200(c)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: FDA will not consider data or analyses submitted after 60 days in determining whether a hearing is warranted unless derived from well-controlled studies begun before the notice and results not available within 60 days; FDA may consider other studies on showing of inadvertent omission and hardship. The requester must list in request for hearing all studies in progress and submit protocol, participating investigators, and brief status report.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Late data generally excluded from threshold hearing determination; exceptions narrow and require showing and advance documentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Other interested persons may submit comments (§314.200(c)(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: Any other interested person not subject to the notice may also submit comments on the proposal to withdraw approval; comments are requested to be submitted within the time and under conditions specified in this section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Non-applicants may provide input but must follow submission timelines/conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to submit studies and raw data for hearing requests (§314.200(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: Person requesting a hearing must submit the studies (including all protocols and underlying raw data) on which they rely to justify a hearing, except when requesting hearing on refusal to approve where relied-upon studies were already submitted in the application in the required format under §314.50.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Complete study data and protocols are required for hearing justification unless already properly included in an application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effectiveness-ground hearings require adequate and well-controlled clinical studies (§314.200(d)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: If grounds concern effectiveness, each request for hearing must be supported only by adequate and well-controlled clinical studies meeting the precise requirements of §314.126 and for combination drug products §300.50, or by other studies for which a waiver has been previously granted. The requester must submit all adequate and well-controlled clinical studies, including unfavorable analyses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Effectiveness contentions must be backed by studies that meet regulatory standards; unfavorable data must be included; no other data may be submitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Point-by-point factual analysis of how studies meet criteria (§314.200(d)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: Submission must include factual analysis specifying how each study accords, on a point-by-point basis, with each criterion required for an adequate well-controlled clinical investigation under §314.126 and, if combination product, requirements of §300.50. If a study concerns a different drug/dosage/form/mode, that must be clearly stated. Studies on the final marketed form must be clearly identified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detailed, explicit mapping between submitted studies and statutory/regulatory criteria is required for each study used to support effectiveness contentions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of required analyses and format for submissions (§314.200(d)(3) and following format I–IV)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each person requesting a hearing shall submit an analysis of the data on which they rely (except safety/effectiveness info may be omitted if not raised by notice). Financial certification/disclosure per part 54 must accompany all clinical data. FDA prefers submissions in the following format: I. Safety data (animal and human, with controlled/uncontrolled, case reports, marketing experiences); II. Effectiveness data (controlled studies with point-by-point analyses); III. Summary of data and medical rationale; IV. Signed statement that submission includes in full all studies and information specified. Warning: willfully false statement is a criminal offense (18 U.S.C. 1001).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FDA provides an explicit organizational format for safety/effectiveness submissions and requires signed verification and financial disclosures; false statements carry criminal penalties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contentions that a product is not a new drug must be raised and supported (§314.200(e))
rubrics_metrics.description: A notice of appearance and request for hearing must contain any contention that the product is not a new drug (e.g., generally recognized as safe and effective under section 201(p), exempt due to marketing before June 25, 1938, or other reasons). Each contention must be supported by a submission under paragraph (d); failure to submit required scientific evidence waives the contention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contentions about legal status of product must be timely raised and supported with the same quantity/quality of evidence required for approval unless a waiver exists; specific documentary formats required for grandfathered/exemption claims (formulation, labeling, marketing, verification).

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence requirements for GRAS/GRAE and pre-1938 ('grandfather') claims (§314.200(e)(1)-(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: A contention that a product is generally recognized as safe and effective must be supported by the same quantity and quality of scientific evidence required to obtain approval unless a waiver applies, and should follow the format/analyses in paragraph (d). A contention of exemption under pre-1938 marketing requires documentary evidence of formulation, labeling, and marketing (with detailed formats for each, and verification statement).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Grandfathering claims demand documentary proof (exact formulations, labeling records, marketing history) and signed verification; lacking these submissions will result in waiver.

rubrics_metrics.name: FDA will not find products identical/related/similar to an approved product exempt (§314.200(e)(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: FDA will not find a product that is identical, related, or similar (as described in §310.6) to a product for which an application is or has been effective, deemed approved, or approved under section 505 to be exempt from part or all new drug provisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proximity to an approved product is a bar to claiming exemption under grandfathering or GRAS/GRAE theories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Separation of functions upon receipt of request for hearing (§314.200(f))
rubrics_metrics.description: Separation of functions starts when a hearing request is received. The Center will prepare analysis and proposed order and submit them plus the request and proposed order denying hearing to the Office of the Commissioner for review. If the Center recommends denial on all issues, no Center representative will participate in the Commissioner's review; if the Center recommends granting on some issues, separation terminates for those issues and Center reps may participate or advise; the Commissioner may modify issue text but cannot deny a hearing on issues recommended for hearing. Separation continues for issues recommended for denial. Participants may move the presiding officer to include excluded issues (ruling reviewable), and failure to move is a waiver. Separation resumes on issuance of notice of hearing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedural firewall to preserve impartial review; parties must move timely to include issues not recommended for hearing or waive those rights.
